meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-19, Time: 08:23 UTC, Duration: 45 min. Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Derek Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Nimbus SRE), Tom Harris (Nimbus Eng Manager), Priya Singh (Nimbus Security)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last week's reliability incidents: intermittent 5xxs and client timeouts during afternoon burst. SE reviewed initial tracers and suggested routing/ retry adjustments; plan to run targeted stress tests and share logs. Agreed to short pilot extension pending results.
topics: Rate limit and retry policy tuning
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Tom: Tom here, good morning.
[00:07] Lina: Lina, SRE, hi.
[00:09] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:11] Derek: Derek from Redwood, SE.
[00:13] Maya: ok great. quick agenda: recap the outages, what we saw in traces, agreed mitigation, and next steps. we have 45.
[01:02] Lina: quick context — between march 14 and 16 we saw a couple of afternoon spikes where client requests started seeing timeouts, some 502/503s, and then a cascade of retries from the client which made it worse.
[01:30] Tom: yeah we ran internal load tests later and couldn't fully reproduce but the production pattern is weird — more likely at 2x normal traffic for a sustained 10–15 minute window.
[01:50] Derek: thanks, i pulled the initial traces from the routing layer and the redwood logs you shared. two things jumped out: a small number of requests were being routed to a model variant that had a higher cold-start tail, and there was a short-lived circuit at the gpu pool level that returned 5xxs while autoscaler spun up additional nodes.
[02:18] Priya: when you say circuit, do you mean a service-level failure not auth? we saw a few alert emails about kube-proxy timeouts.
[02:28] Derek: yeah that's right — the 5xxs appear service-side; not auth. some of the 5xxs are internal kernel errors on the inferencer process; others are gateway timeout when the node got overloaded.
[03:01] Lina: we also noticed the customer-side client had an aggressive immediate retry loop which amplified the load. should we be doing client-side backoff recommendations?
[03:14] Maya: yes that's one of the easy mitigations. we recommended exponential backoff with jitter in the docs, but we can share a snippet. i'll send that.
[03:25] Derek: also, quick mitigation on our side — we turned on per-route soft rate limits and a slightly longer request timeout for that route to avoid premature client retries. that reduced 5xxs in the canary.
[03:40] Tom: did you change model routing? because we also saw a variant mix where smaller quantized model got more traffic.
[03:47] Derek: correct — the smart router had a fallback policy to a smaller quantized variant for cost, but when capacity is constrained it can accidentally route requests to a model with longer tail under burst. we recommend pinning the route to a single variant during the pilot burst tests.
[04:12] Lina: ok, that makes sense. what's the recommended retry policy on the client to avoid thundering herds?
[04:20] Derek: exponential backoff starting at 200ms, cap at 2s, max 3 retries, and use jitter. also include idempotency keys for replays where applicable.
[04:33] Priya: from a security/compliance lens, we also need to ensure logs we share are redacted. we'll need the SOC2 docs before we move forward.
[04:42] Maya: absolutely — i'll attach SOC2 and our security whitepaper and a trimmed log guide.
[05:00] Derek: on root cause, there were two contributing factors: autoscaler lag + client retry amplification + a small fraction of requests hitting a model variant with higher latency tail. individually not fatal, together they caused the 5xx/timeouts.
[05:25] Tom: the autoscaler lag — is that config on your side or ours? we run the dedicated-like pool in the pilot though you've said it's a shared test pool.
[05:36] Derek: autoscaler lives in the serving runtime managed by Redwood during the hosted pilot; config we control but we can expose tuning knobs. for the pilot we can increase min pool size and reduce scale-up cooldown.
[05:52] Lina: okay we want higher baseline for afternoon window, especially on weekdays.
[05:58] Derek: noted — i can provision a temporary higher min for the next stress test.
[06:08] Maya: let's talk test plan — derek?
[06:11] Derek: propose a 2-hour stress test at 50rps which matches two times your average plus a 15 minute sustained burst at 120rps to simulate the observed window. we'll run:
[06:28] - single-model pinned run (no fallback)
[06:32] - routing with fallback enabled
[06:35] - client retry patterns: immediate retries vs exponential backoff
[06:40] we'll capture full traces, per-node metrics, and request IDs. i'll share results and a spreadsheet.
[06:49] Tom: timeline?
[06:50] Derek: i can run the tests tomorrow but need your signoff on a maintenance window. if confirmed i'll run 08:00–10:00 UTC.
[06:58] Lina: tomorrow 08:00 is ok for us. we'll provide a lightweight smoke harness that mimics our client shuffle.
[07:06] Priya: please redact PII from traces; we only need timings and error codes.
[07:11] Derek: understood, we'll strip payloads and only keep hashes and timing metadata.
[07:18] Maya: pricing/contract — maya speaks: given the incident we agreed to a one-week pilot extension while we run tests. i'll send an addendum and updated pricing for the dedicated-like baseline.
[07:31] Tom: fine. any blockers on our side for the test?
[07:33] Lina: none beyond logs export which we'll do after this call.
[07:37] Derek: also want to check the SDK usage — are you using our official sdk or homegrown wrapper?
[07:42] Tom: homegrown wrapper that calls the http api; we can add the recommended retry logic quickly.
[07:47] Derek: ok we'll send a code snippet for backoff and idempotency keys.
[08:00] Maya: priya, any security asks beyond SOC2?
[08:03] Priya: KMS integration notes and audit retention policy — we'll need the retention window and whether logs can be shipped to our splunk.
[08:11] Maya: we support customer KMS in private deployment; for hosted pilot we can redact and ship logs to your splunk via a secure syslog endpoint — i'll include options.
[08:23] Derek: quick note on metrics — enable token-level latency distribution in the console and set an alert threshold for p95 > 1.2s. that helped us catch tail in other pilots.
[08:37] Lina: got it, we'll create an alert.
[08:42] Tom: any other competitors or alternatives discussed?
[08:44] Maya: customer mentioned anthropic and some internal bedrock evals, but they liked our observability and routing controls.
[08:53] Priya: ok next steps recap?
[08:55] Maya: derek runs stress test 08:00–10:00 tomorrow, lina shares logs from march 14–16, maya sends security docs and pricing, customer will add client backoff and run smoke harness. agreed?
[09:10] Tom: agreed.
[09:12] Lina: agreed.
[09:13] Priya: thanks all.
[09:15] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll follow up in email with links: bench spreadsheet, security pack, and the code snippet.
[09:25] End of call.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present — product names sometimes mismatched ("kv cache" transcribed as "k v cash" in the raw logs). Shared artifacts: https://redwood.app/notes/poc/nimbus-health-bench (benchmark spreadsheet), https://redwood.app/security/soc2.pdf (security pack).
